android.title: On Android, nothing to configure
android.installed: In your gallery, select photos, tap Share, then choose Maisonnée. The token below is only useful for an iPhone.
android.toInstall: First install Maisonnée on your home screen: « Maisonnée » will then appear in your gallery’s Share menu. The token below is only useful for an iPhone.

ios.title: On iPhone, in three steps
ios.step1: Create a token below and copy it.
ios.step2: In the Shortcuts app, create a shortcut shown in the share sheet, accepting images.
ios.step3: Add « Repeat with Each » over the shortcut input, and inside it « Get Contents of URL » pointing at your instance, method POST, with the Authorization header set to « Device » followed by your token, a Form request body, a file field of type File set to the repeat item, and a type field set to photo.
ios.warning: Two pitfalls: the request body must be Form and not JSON, and the type field must be photo — without it the picture never reaches the gallery.

create-zone.title: Describe your home in zones
create-zone.description: Create your rooms, floors or buildings: zones provide context across the whole app.

add-equipment.title: Add a first piece of equipment
add-equipment.description: Boiler, ventilation, appliances… register equipment to track warranty and maintenance.

first-task.title: Create your first task
first-task.description: Write down something to do, assign it and give it a due date.

log-note.title: Write a note in the journal
log-note.description: The journal keeps track of everything happening in the household.

ask-agent.title: Ask the assistant a question
ask-agent.description: Try asking "how much did we spend this month?" — it answers with sources.

invite-member.title: Invite a household member
invite-member.description: From settings, create an invitation link and send it to your family yourself.

declare-account.title: Declare an account and its starting point
declare-account.description: An account, its opening balance and the matching date: that is the prerequisite for all money tracking. Without it, no check covers your expenses.

dashboard.title: Discover the dashboard
dashboard.intro: The dashboard gives you an overview of your household as soon as you log in.

overview.title: Read the overview
overview.body: Cards summarise each module: ongoing tasks, latest expenses, recent readings…

activity.title: Follow the activity feed
activity.body: The feed shows the latest household journal entries: notes, expenses, maintenance.

alerts.title: Keep an eye on alerts
alerts.body: The header bell flags what needs your attention; the Alerts page has the details.

search.title: Search everything at once
search.body: The box in the top bar (⌘K) searches every document, task, project or expense your household holds.

agent.title: Use the AI assistant
agent.intro: The assistant answers questions about your household data in plain language, with verifiable sources.

ask.title: Ask a question
ask.body: The assistant is reachable everywhere via the floating ✨ button (bottom-right), or the Agent page. Ask, for example, "which tasks are overdue?".

citations.title: Check the sources
citations.body: Every answer cites the items it used; click a citation to open the item.

web.title: Let it search the web
web.body: When available, the 🌐 button by the input lets the assistant search the internet if your household data isn't enough. It's off by default, set per conversation, and the assistant decides when to search.

context.title: Give it context
context.body: Open the assistant from a detail page: it anchors on the current item. Switch between "This page" and "Whole household", and the "What I know" panel shows what it already knows — use "Add context" to point it at another project, note or equipment.

create.title: Create from the chat
create.body: Ask "create a task…" or "note that…": the item is created immediately, with an Undo button.

memory.title: Manage memory
memory.body: The assistant remembers durable facts about you; review and delete them from the Memory page.

zones.title: Organise your home into zones
zones.intro: Zones (rooms, floors, buildings) structure navigation across the whole app.

create.title: Create your zones
create.body: Add your main rooms: kitchen, living room, garage, garden…

hierarchy.title: Build the hierarchy
hierarchy.body: Nest zones (floor → bedroom) to mirror your home.

read.title: Read a row
read.body: On the right of each zone: its area and its counters (sub-zones, equipment, open tasks, active projects); a missing counter means zero. Busy zones and empty ones stand out without opening anything.

find.title: Collapse and search
find.body: Collapse the branches you don't need, and type in the search field to go straight to a zone: the parents of a match stay visible, so you never lose the context.

order.title: Put them in your order
order.body: Drag a zone by its handle, or use “Move up” / “Move down” in its ⋯ menu: your order applies everywhere, forms included.

navigate.title: Navigate by zone
navigate.body: A zone's page gathers the equipment, tasks and events attached to it.

equipment.title: Track your equipment
equipment.intro: Warranty, servicing, history: everything about a piece of equipment in one place.

add.title: Add equipment
add.body: A name, a category and a zone are enough. The rest — serial number, purchase, warranty, servicing — lives in collapsible sections, to fill in the day you have the information at hand.

service.title: Mark a service as done
service.body: Set a service interval (in months) and the app works out the next due date. When the day comes, “Mark as serviced” dates the service and records it in the household log in one click — the alert clears itself.

purchase.title: Record an expense
purchase.body: A part, a repair, a consumable: the expense is created in the household log and linked to the equipment. The record itself is left untouched.

history.title: Browse the history
history.body: Services, expenses and interventions linked to the equipment all show up together on its detail page.

electricity.title: Model your electrical installation
electricity.intro: Describe the electrical panel and track your consumption.

board.title: Describe the panel
board.body: Create the panel, its breakers and circuits, then link them to usage points.

readings.title: Enter readings
readings.body: Regularly add your meter index, or import a readings file. Save your provider's download link on the meter: the import dialog then opens it in one click.

analyze.title: Analyse consumption
analyze.body: Charts aggregate your readings by period to spot drifts.

water.title: Track water consumption
water.intro: Manual meter readings are enough to follow your water consumption.

readings.title: Enter a reading
readings.body: Note the date and the index in m³; regular readings give reliable curves.

charts.title: Read the charts
charts.body: Browse by period and compare consumption, just like electricity.

weather.title: Track your home's weather
weather.intro: See your home's local weather — today's conditions and a 7-day forecast.

location.title: Set your location
location.body: In Settings > your household, the “Weather location” field, search for your city to enable the module.

forecast.title: Check the forecast
forecast.body: The Weather page shows current conditions, how today evolves, and a 7-day forecast.

dashboard.title: A glance from the dashboard
dashboard.body: A weather summary shows on the dashboard, and the current temperature in the header: click either to open the full page.

alerts.title: Get weather alerts
alerts.body: On the Alerts page you see weather risks (frost, heatwave, wind, storm). Enable the weather ping in Settings for a proactive Telegram + bell alert.

stock.title: Manage household stock
stock.intro: Consumables and supplies: quantities, categories and expiry dates under control.

add.title: Create items
add.body: Add your consumables (pet food, bulbs, firewood…) with their unit.

quantities.title: Adjust quantities
quantities.body: Update quantities as you buy and consume; a purchase creates its expense automatically.

expiry.title: Watch expiry dates
expiry.body: Fill in expiry dates to be alerted before it's too late.

shopping.title: Keep a shopping list
shopping.intro: One shared list the whole household ticks off — free-text, from your stock, or via the assistant.

quickAdd.title: Add what you need
quickAdd.body: Type an item in the quick-add box and press Add. It appears instantly for everyone in the household.

fromStock.title: Add from your stock
fromStock.body: On any stock item, use "Add to shopping list" — the line is linked to that item and the suggested quantity refills it. Adding it twice won't create a duplicate.

check.title: Tick it off while shopping
check.body: Check an item to cross it out and move it to "Picked up". "Clear picked" empties that section (with an undo).

agent.title: Let the assistant fill it
agent.body: Just say "add coffee to the list" — the assistant adds it, links it to your stock when it recognises the name, and you can undo in one tap.

suggestions.title: Restock what's running low
suggestions.body: The Suggestions section proposes stock items below their threshold — add them in one tap, with a refill quantity prefilled.

commit.title: Log purchases back to stock
commit.body: Once shopping, tick items off then use “Save to stock” to record the purchase — it restocks the item (creating it if needed) and logs the expense.

chickens.title: Keep the chicken coop
chickens.intro: Flock register, daily egg log and cost per egg.

flock.title: Register your hens
flock.body: Create a record per hen: name, breed, arrival date.

eggs.title: Log the eggs
eggs.body: Enter the number of eggs collected each day — the history builds itself.

events.title: Record events
events.body: Care, brooding, moulting, death: each hen's record keeps its timeline.

chores.title: Never wonder when you last cleaned
chores.body: Add the jobs you redo — clean the coop, wash the feeder — with how many days apart. Tick « Done » each time and Maisonnée counts from there; turn on the coop reminder in Settings › Proactive messages and it tells you in the morning when one has slipped.

stats.title: Track laying and cost
stats.body: Pick a period for the laying curve: un-logged days never show as 0, and the coverage rate stays visible. Cost per egg (feed + care) and an abnormal-drop alert (molt, weather) round it out.

media.title: Photos & documents
media.body: Open the Photos or Documents tab on a hen to attach before/after photos or papers (vet, invoice). Upload a new file or connect an existing one — the tab appears via the « + » menu until it holds something.

insurance.title: Track your insurance
insurance.intro: All household contracts (home, health, car…) in one place.

contracts.title: Add your contracts
contracts.body: Fill in the insurer, type, number and renewal date of each contract.

documents.title: Attach documents
documents.body: Link PDF contracts and certificates from the Documents module.

tasks.title: Manage tasks
tasks.intro: The household to-do list: assignment, due dates and follow-up.

create.title: Create a task
create.body: A title is enough; add a due date, a zone and an assignee if needed.

organize.title: Filter and organise
organize.body: Filters (to do, overdue, done…) keep the list readable.

weather.title: Plan around the weather
weather.body: Mark an outdoor task as “needs dry weather” and its detail suggests the dry days ahead.

complete.title: Complete and find again
complete.body: Check a task to complete it; the history remains available.

projects.title: Run a project
projects.intro: Renovation, purchase, holidays: follow a project end to end with budget and expenses.

create.title: Create the project
create.body: Give it a name, a description and a planned budget.

plan.title: Gather tasks and notes
plan.body: Link tasks, notes and documents to the project — the detail page only shows the tabs that have content, with a « + » menu to open the others.

photos.title: Document before / after
photos.body: In the Photos tab, upload pictures and tag them before, during or after — then open the comparator to see the transformation side by side.

budget.title: Track the budget
budget.body: Linked expenses feed the actual cost, automatically compared to the budget.

interactions.title: Keep the household journal
interactions.intro: The log records what happens to the household: notes, maintenance, repairs, callouts. Expenses have a module of their own.

log.title: Add an entry
log.body: Record a note or a callout in seconds from the Activity page.

types.title: Pick the right type
types.body: Note, maintenance, repair, warranty… the type says what it is and acts as a filter. Expenses do not appear here: they live in the Money module, where they carry a budget and the statement that accounts for them.

link.title: Link to context
link.body: Attach zones, documents or tasks to an entry to find it back easily.

trackers.title: Track values over time
trackers.intro: Meter readings, weight, tank level: dated value series with charts.

create.title: Create a tracker
create.body: Pick a name and a unit (kg, m³, hours…).

entries.title: Add values
entries.body: Enter a dated value at each reading; the series builds up.

charts.title: Read the trend
charts.body: The tracker's chart shows the trend; a tracker can also live inside a project.

expenses.title: Track expenses
expenses.intro: All household expenses, entered by hand or created automatically by purchases.

record.title: Enter an expense
record.body:
Restaurant, gift, groceries: the « New expense » button opens the same form from the dashboard and from the Expenses tab. There are no longer two of them writing different things.

The only question that changes anything is: how did you pay?

In cash, the expense becomes a real operation on your cash account. Nothing is ever imported onto a cash account, so what you type is the truth — there is no discrepancy to wait for.

By card, transfer or direct debit, no account line is created. The expense waits for the statement, which will match it on import. That is normal, and the Control tab does not hold it against you until that period's statement has arrived.

supplier.title: Pick a supplier, never retype one
supplier.body:
The supplier field is a searchable list built from your own entries, most-used first. An unknown shop is simply typed in — it joins the list for next time, with no form to fill in.

Case and accents no longer create duplicates: "leroy merlin" lands on "Leroy Merlin". That is what keeps one filter and one total per shop, where three spellings used to give three.

When you split a statement line, the app also offers the merchant read from the operation label — so the common case takes no typing at all.

You can also fix several expenses at once: "Select" above the list, tick the ones you want, then "Edit…". The same gesture changes the budget too — the quickest way to empty the list of expenses without an envelope that the Control tab reports. The batch goes in one go: if anything is wrong, nothing is written.

sources.title: Understand automatic expenses
sources.body: Stock or equipment purchases create their expense on their own — nothing to re-enter.

review.title: Analyse by period
review.body: Filter by period or by zone to see where the money goes.

sort.title: Sort your operations
sort.body: The “To sort” tab lists every outflow nobody has accounted for yet. A budget pill covers the common case; “Split into several” is there when one shop trip spans two categories. Select several lines to handle a batch at once.

control.title: Check that your figures are right
control.body: The “Control” tab lists everything standing between you and accurate figures: unaccounted operations, expenses the bank never saw, balances that do not chain. Each one is resolved — or arbitrated with a motive that stays visible and revocable.

trace.title: Trace it back to the operation
trace.body: Every expense shows whether a statement line accounts for it. “Statement of 12 July” is a link: it takes you to the operation, with its amount, its account, and the other expenses it covers. “Awaiting reconciliation” means the opposite — an expense the bank never saw, which is a discrepancy the Control tab counts. Nothing shows outside the checked period: there, the app cannot require anything.

sheet.title: An expense's sheet
sheet.body: Click an expense: its sheet opens. It answers three questions — how much and to whom, which envelope the euro falls into, and what justifies it. An expense with no envelope says so and offers to pick one. An expense born from a statement shows the other expenses on the same transaction, so €90 on a €150 outflow doesn't look like a mistake. Edit, delete, attach to a line, add a receipt: all from there.

documents.title: File your documents
documents.intro: Invoices, manuals, certificates: household files, linked to their context.

upload.title: Upload a file
upload.body: Upload a PDF or an image — several files at once if you have a whole batch. A file uploaded on its own can be given a clear title; in a batch, each keeps its own.

link.title: Link to the right object
link.body: Attach the document to a piece of equipment, a contract or a project.

find.title: Find a document again
find.body: Filter by type in one click, group by type or date, search inside file text — the AI assistant can find them too.

photos.title: Browse photos
photos.intro: A dedicated view of household photos, fed by the Documents module.

browse.title: Browse the gallery
browse.body: Images uploaded to Documents show up here, grouped by month. Filter by zone to focus on one room, and once a photo is open the arrows (or ← →) move to the next one without closing it.

sort.title: Say why a photo exists
sort.body: A serial-number photo and a birthday photo have no business sitting in the same place. Give each one its purpose: Technical (proof you will read again), Observation (a dated fact — a crack, a leak) or Memory. The gallery then filters on one of them. A photo nobody sorted stays in « To sort » — that is a state, not a memory by default.

add.title: Add photos
add.body: Pick a whole series at once: the field accepts several photos, sent one after another. From a project, a piece of equipment or a zone, the Photos tab sorts them into Before / During / After and can compare them.

file.title: File a photo into a zone
file.body: The crossed-out location icon on the open photo flags a photo filed nowhere, and the “No zone” filter gathers them all in the gallery. Assign a zone without leaving the gallery: from the ⋯ menu on the thumbnail, or by expanding the info card of the open photo — the same fold lets you fix its title. To file several at once, hit “Select” and tick them: the zones you pick are added to those already set.

phone.title: Send from your phone
phone.body: The most common move is not opening Maisonnée to import, it is having just taken a picture. On Android, install the app on your home screen and « Maisonnée » appears in the Share menu: nothing else to do. On iPhone, create a token under Settings → Devices, then a shortcut that sends the photos — the steps are shown on that screen when you open it from your phone.

directory.title: Build the address book
directory.intro: Craftsmen, neighbours, services: the household's useful contacts, shared with all members.

contacts.title: Add contacts
contacts.body: Name, phone, email, notes: create a record per person.

structures.title: Register organisations
structures.body: Companies, administrations, associations — link their contacts to them.

alerts.title: Handle alerts
alerts.intro: Alerts gather what needs your attention: expiry dates, deadlines, warranties…

review.title: Review them
review.body: The header bell surfaces current alerts; the page lists them by type.

act.title: Act on an alert
act.body: Open the related item from the alert and fix the cause: the alert goes away.

settings.title: Configure the app and household
settings.intro: Profile, appearance, members and modules: everything is configured in settings.

profile.title: Personalise your profile
profile.body: Display name, language, light/dark theme and colour palette.

household.title: Manage the household
household.body: Invite members and manage roles; the household name at the top of the screen switches between them.

invite.title: Invite the household
invite.body: Invite creates a link — Maisonnée sends no email. Copy it and pass it on however you like: whoever opens it chooses a password and lands straight in the household, with no account needed beforehand. An email address is optional and only addresses the invitation. A link lasts a week, and you can revoke it at any time.

modules.title: Enable the right modules
modules.body: Disable modules you don't need (chicken coop, insurance…) to lighten the navigation.

capabilities.title: See what this instance can do
capabilities.body: Assistant, semantic search, email, push notifications, Telegram: these depend on keys set when the app was installed, not on a household setting. The list shows which ones are on, what you lose without the others, and links to how each is enabled.

digest.title: Get your daily digest
digest.intro: Let the assistant speak first: a short daily recap of what needs your attention, pushed to Telegram.

preview.title: See today's digest
preview.body: Open the Daily digest page to preview what today's recap contains — tasks due, weather alerts, low stock and more.

enable.title: Turn on delivery
enable.body: Link your Telegram account, then enable the digest and pick the time you want to receive it each morning.

sections.title: Choose your sections
sections.body: Tick only the topics you care about. Sections for modules you don't use are hidden automatically.

install.title: Install the app & get notifications
install.intro: Add the house to your phone's home screen and receive its notifications as push, even when the app is closed.

install.title: Add to your home screen
install.body: On iPhone (Safari): tap Share, then "Add to Home Screen". On Android or desktop: use the browser's install button. Then open the app from that icon.

enable.title: Turn on push notifications
enable.body: In Settings, open "Push notifications", tap Enable and allow the permission. Use Test to check a notification reaches your device.

badge.title: Badge on the icon
badge.body: Unread notifications show as a count on the app icon, cleared when you read them. On iPhone this works only from the installed app (iOS 16.4+).

budget.title: Budgets
budget.intro: Sort your spending into categories, and set a monthly ceiling wherever you want one.

create.title: Create a budget
create.body: Tap “New budget” and give it a name (e.g. Groceries). The monthly ceiling is optional: leave it empty to simply track a category like “Gifts”. Add a global budget to cap your spending as a whole — that one does need an amount.

assign.title: Attach expenses
assign.body: When you add a manual expense, pick a budget to count it against. Expenses left unassigned show up under "Unbudgeted".

track.title: Track the month
track.body: Each capped budget shows spent vs ceiling with a progress bar — amber near the limit, red once over. A category with no ceiling shows its total only. Counters reset every month. Tap a budget to see the expenses its counter is made of — “Unbudgeted” opens the same way. The bar comes in two shades: the solid part is what a statement line attests to, the pale part what is still awaiting reconciliation. The counter itself counts everything — yesterday's expense is real even before the statement is imported. A refund (returned item, reimbursed fee) is deducted: the counter shows the net, and the refund line appears under the expenses.

sheet.title: Open a budget's sheet
sheet.body:
Tap a budget to open its sheet. Pick the period — the four shortcuts, or two free dates — and everything recomputes. Under the amount sits the comparison with the equivalent previous period: a month compares with the month before, a year with the year before, a free window with the same duration just before it. Below that, the spending rhythm day by day (month by month over a long window) and each supplier's share as a percentage. With nothing spent before, Maisonnée says there is no comparison rather than inventing a percentage. « Unbudgeted » opens exactly the same way.

At the bottom, the period's expenses are browsed page by page. « Select » ticks several lines, then « Fix… » changes their supplier or their budget in one go — that is how you move what sits in the wrong envelope. Moved lines leave the sheet right away: they now count elsewhere. The chips above the list narrow it down — a kind, a supplier, or « without supplier » to spot what is still to be filled in. They leave the total at the top alone: it keeps covering the whole period, because that is the figure compared with the ceiling.

analysis.title: See where it actually goes
analysis.body: Open “Spending analysis” from the budget page: each category month by month, the breakdown over 6, 12 or 24 months, the suppliers that weigh most and your biggest expenses. This is where a drifting category shows up — the Budgets panel only ever looks at the current month.

recurring.title: Anticipate recurring bills
recurring.body: Open “Recurring expenses” from the budget page to log subscriptions, insurance and bills. See what falls due over the next 30/90 days, and confirm each occurrence in one click when paid (the amount is editable) — it lands in your journal and advances to the next date.

report.title: Read your monthly report
report.body: On the 5th working day of the month, a written recap of the previous month is generated: total spent, how each budget did, biggest expenses, recurring bills paid and the trend versus the month before. The delay leaves time to enter the month's last expenses. Find it under “Monthly report” on the budget page — in your language, with the raw figures as a fallback when no AI key is set.

banking.title: Accounts
banking.intro: Declare your accounts once — they're the foundation your bank statements will build on.

accounts.title: Add your accounts
accounts.body: Tap “New account” and create one per bank. The name is how you'll tell them apart; add the bank and the last 4 characters of the IBAN if you hold two accounts at the same institution. The full IBAN is never stored.

cash.title: Track cash too
cash.body: Create a “Cash” account for the household's physical money. It works like a bank account, and cash enters it two ways: “Feed cash” on a withdrawal line, and “Cash in” on the Accounts tab for money from elsewhere (a gift, a sale, a friend's share). A cash spend becomes an operation on that account — an expense the control can reconcile, like any other. If you pour only part of a withdrawal into the pot, the Control tells you: the rest would belong nowhere.

openingBalance.title: Set the starting balance
openingBalance.body: Enter the account balance at a given date — typically the one on the first statement you plan to import. It is required, for a good reason: without a starting point the balance shown would be a guess, and no conformity check would cover this account. It can be negative if you are overdrawn.

import.title: Import your first statement
import.body: On the account card, pick “Import a statement” and drop your bank's CSV or Excel export. Set once which column holds the date, the label and the amount — and if your bank also exports the running balance, map it: that's what tells two identical same-day operations apart and reveals a missing statement. The mapping is remembered, so next time you just drop the file. Re-importing the same statement never creates duplicates.

journal.title: Browse, qualify, classify
journal.body: From the Accounts tab, open “Bank journal”: every line, filterable by account, period, direction and label. Three useful gestures: flag an internal movement (a withdrawal is not spending), classify a receipt (wage, refund, internal transfer — the three do not mean the same thing), and annotate a line.

balance.title: Check your balance
balance.body: Each account shows its balance, computed at read time — never frozen in the database. If your bank exports a balance column, Maisonnée anchors on it and checks the statement chain along the way: when operations are missing you get “chain broken” with the period and the missing amount, rather than a plausible but wrong figure. This is the best test of your imports: if the balance shown matches your paper statement, everything is right. For cash, open the journal and use “Move to cash” on a withdrawal — it leaves the spending totals and feeds your cash account balance.

sheet.title: Open an account's sheet
sheet.body: Tap an account's name to open its sheet. Everything Maisonnée knows about it is gathered there: its balance and where that figure comes from, the **checked period** (outside it Maisonnée requires nothing — before is history, after is a statement that has not arrived yet), the periods no statement ever covered, the full history of your imports with what each one created, skipped and reconciled by itself, and how many operations are still waiting to be sorted out on this account. If the sheet says no check applies to this account, fix it right there: it is the one setting that makes every other check meaningful.

money.title: How money works here
money.intro: Understand before clicking. The Money module follows a few rules that are not obvious — and one of them explains why not everything is always flagged.

source.title: The statement is the truth, not your memory
source.body: A statement line is a fact: the bank wrote it, the app never rewrites it. Everything else leans on it. That is why importing your statements is not paperwork but the foundation: without them, the app can only take your word for it.

allocation.title: An expense gives a line its meaning
allocation.body: A line says “42 € left for Leclerc”. It does not say *why*. The expense is you saying “that was groceries”. Assigning a budget from “To sort” is exactly that — there is no extra step to create the expense, it is the same gesture.

axes.title: A line can be split, along two axes
axes.body: 150 € at the DIY store, 90 € of it for the bathroom and 60 € unrelated: you split the line in two. And each part carries two independent facts — a budget (“DIY”) and an object (the bathroom job). Those 90 € therefore count in your envelope *and* in the job's cost, which is not double counting: they answer two different questions.

window.title: Why not everything is checked
window.body:
The app only flags what you can actually fix. So it defines a checking period per account: from your opening balance date up to the last imported statement. Before that: history, and no bank line will ever come to match it. After that: the statement simply has not arrived yet. Between the two, the requirement is total — and that is what makes “zero discrepancy” reachable.

One consequence worth knowing. If your opening balance date is later than your operations, the period is empty and nothing at all is checked. The app then says so explicitly, instead of letting you believe all is well.

And if you do not know that past balance — many banks never export it — do not guess it: « Find the opening balance » asks for the balance you can read today and subtracts the movements for you.

arbitrate.title: Arbitrating is not hiding
arbitrate.body:
Some discrepancies are legitimate: bank fees belonging to no budget, a purchase someone else paid for. You “arbitrate” them — with a mandatory motive. The discrepancy leaves your worklist but stays readable, and you can revoke the arbitration in one click: it comes back identical.

And an arbitration expires. If you wrote “the rest of this line does not interest me” and then change its split, the discrepancy reappears: your motive no longer described the situation.

notEvaluable.title: A zero can mean two things
notEvaluable.body:
“Nothing to report” means: the check ran, all is well. “Not evaluable” means: the check could not run, because a prerequisite is missing — typically an account with no opening balance, or one whose date falls outside its own operations.

The app never conflates the two. A non-evaluable check shows a dash, not a zero, and names the prerequisite to clear. Fix it, and everything becomes measurable at once.

cash.title: Cash is an account like any other
cash.body: A note handed over at the market leaves no statement line. So that it does not become an expense the bank never saw — a discrepancy nobody can resolve — the app records it as an operation on your “Cash” account. Feed it with your withdrawals, and your physical money is tracked like the rest.

recap.title: Your monthly recap
recap.intro: Every module in Maisonnée asks you for something. This is the one page that gives something back: once a month, your household's month told in a handful of cards.

what.title: What it is
what.body: On the 5th working day of the month, Maisonnée closes the month just gone and tells it: what you spent, what you got done, what the house consumed, what you photographed. The first days of the month give you time to record the last receipts — after that there is nothing to fill in, it is built from what you already recorded.

story.title: Read it like a story
story.body: Cards come one screen at a time: one figure, one sentence. Move with the buttons, the dots, or the ← → arrows; press Escape to leave. Earlier months stay in the list below — no need to replay them.

chapters.title: Choose your chapters
chapters.body: Turn off any chapter you would rather not be told about. Muting never erases: turn it back on and past months read in full again. Chapters whose module is off never appear at all.

appointment.title: Get told when it's ready
appointment.body: Enable the reminder and Maisonnée messages you on the 5th working day of the month with a link. It is off by default: if you already receive the monthly budget report, you would otherwise get two messages that morning.

frozen.title: Why the figures never move
frozen.body: A recap is frozen the first time it is read, and never recomputed. Correct an expense from June in August and June's recap keeps the figures it had — that is what makes it a memory rather than a query.

orchard.title: Keep your orchard
orchard.intro: What you did to each tree, what it gave, and what the season is asking for.

subjects.title: Plant your subjects
subjects.body: One record per tree, bush or vine. A zone is required: an orchard is found by place.

journal.title: Log what you do
journal.body: Pruning, treatment, observation — dated and typed. A tree answers a year later; your memory does not.

seasons.title: Say when, not how often
seasons.body: « Winter pruning runs November to March. » The page opens on what the season asks for; mark it done, or turn it into a task.

harvests.title: Weigh your harvests
harvests.body: Record every picking. Fruit trees alternate: it is the run of seasons that speaks, never a single year.

frost.title: Protect blossom from frost
frost.body: Set a subject's flowering window: a frost night forecast during it is flagged the day before. Without it, no alert.

agent.title: Ask the assistant
agent.body: « How many kilos of apples this year? », or dictate « log 12 kg of apples on the far apple tree ».

games.title: Play a treasure hunt
games.intro: The one game that is not played on a screen: the app writes the trail, the house holds it.

labels.title: Print and stick the labels
labels.body: One QR label per room, printed from the Rooms page and taped to the wall. Nothing works without them — scanning one outside a game simply opens that room.

compose.title: Compose a trail
compose.body: Pick a few rooms, one riddle each, and write what is hidden at the end. The order of the list is the order of the game.

riddles.title: Ask for riddles
riddles.body: The assistant writes one riddle per room, tuned to the players' age. You read them over and fix what you want before saving. No key configured? Write them yourself — everything else is the same.

play.title: Hand over the phone
play.body: Start the hunt and give the phone away. Each correct scan reveals the next riddle; a wrong room says nothing. The last one reveals the treasure.

replay.title: Bring it back out
replay.body: A finished hunt replays in a shuffled order, as a new draft. The original stays untouched — it is the trace that you played.

privacy.title: Before you start
privacy.intro: The agent reads the data of your household to answer your questions. A few things to know:
privacy.point_provider: Your questions and the matching excerpts are sent to Anthropic (Claude) to generate the answer.
privacy.point_scope: Only data from your household is shared, never data from another household.
privacy.point_retention: Your conversations are saved to your account so you can pick them up later — you can delete them at any time. Usage stats (latency, success) are logged without the content of your questions.

errors.sourceIncomplete: Pick the object to attach, or set it back to “Nothing”.

linked.title: Expenses already attached
linked.hint: Reconciled elsewhere: they count against this operation but are not edited here.

reconcile.title: Reconcile this operation
reconcile.noSuggestion: No recorded expense matches this operation.
reconcile.pickExisting: Attach an expense you already recorded
reconcile.pickExistingHint: Expenses the bank never confirmed, that fit in the {{amount}} still free.
reconcile.noUnreconciled: No unreconciled expense fits in what is left.
reconcile.alreadyTyped_one: 1 expense already typed fits in this line
reconcile.alreadyTyped_other: {{count}} expenses already typed fit in this line

inflow.title: Classify this receipt
inflow.hint: “Other” is a choice; leaving it blank means “not looked at yet”, which the control reports.
inflow.refundBudgetHint: Split the credited amount across the envelopes it refunds. Whatever is left unassigned stays reported by the Control tab.

errors.budgetRequired: Pick a budget for every credited amount.
errors.amountInvalid: Every credited amount must be above zero.
errors.overCredited: This refund only brought {{total}}: it cannot credit more.

anchor.title: Find the opening balance
anchor.intro: Your bank does not export balances in its statements. Give the balance you can read today: Maisonnée subtracts the movements to find the starting one.
anchor.noLines: This account holds no operation. Import a statement first, or type the opening balance straight into the account.
anchor.fromStatement: Your statement carries the balance — nothing to type.
anchor.fromStatementDetail: Maisonnée read {{amount}} on {{date}} in your operations. Nothing estimated: that is the bank's own figure.
anchor.balanceHint: The balance as your banking app shows it. An overdraft goes in as a negative number.
anchor.confirmLast: I confirm the last operation on my online statement is this one:
anchor.computation: {{balance}} read, minus {{movements}} of movements over the period.
anchor.gapDetail: Nothing was imported from {{start}} to {{end}}. The movements to subtract are incomplete: import that statement first, or the balance found would be off by the missing amount.
anchor.attestedOn: Reconstructed from a balance of {{amount}} read on {{date}}

errors.beforeLastLine: You hold operations more recent than that balance. Read it again, after them.
errors.future: That date has not happened yet.
errors.periodGap: A period of the interval was never imported: the movements to subtract are incomplete.
errors.noLines: This account holds no operation to subtract.

transaction.noAllocation: Nothing is attached to this operation yet.

attach.title: Attach to an operation
attach.hint: Only operations whose remaining amount covers this expense are listed. An expense may cover just part of a line: the rest will wait for its own allocation.
attach.none: No operation has room for this amount. Import the period's statement, or check the expense amount.
attach.ownedHint: This expense *is* the operation's allocation: removing it sends the line back to the queue. The operation itself is never touched.
attach.removeSplitHint: Deletes this expense; the bank operation is untouched and goes back to the queue.

deposit.title: Cash coming in
deposit.labelPlaceholder: E.g. gift, bike sold, Marie's share
deposit.natureHint: An internal transfer is not recorded here: cash from a withdrawal is declared on the withdrawal line, with “Feed cash”.

account.archivedHint: This account is archived: it no longer shows in the list and its balance is no longer tracked. Nothing was deleted — you can reopen it.
account.balanceUnavailable: No balance computed for this account.
account.coverageHint: Outside it, Maisonnée requires nothing: before is history, after is a statement that has not arrived yet.

coverageNone.no_opening_date: No opening balance date: no check applies to this account.
coverageNone.opening_date_after_data: Your opening balance date ({{openingDate}}) is later than your oldest operation ({{earliestLine}}): the checked period is empty, so no check applies to this account.
coverageNone.no_data: No operation on this account yet, so there is nothing to check. Import a statement to open the period.

account.flowTitle: What came in and went out
account.flowHint: The bank view, over the whole history of the account. These totals are never added to budget totals: the bridge is the coverage ratio.
account.pendingCount_one: {{count}} operation still to sort out on this account
account.pendingCount_other: {{count}} operations still to sort out on this account
account.pendingNone: Nothing left to sort out on this account.
account.noImportsCash: A cash account has no statement: its operations are typed in by hand.

history.title: Balance over time
history.tooShort: Not enough history yet to draw a curve.
history.unreliable: A gap in the statement chain shifts the whole earlier part of this curve — the shape looks normal but the figures before the gap are off.

transfer.title: The other leg of this transfer
transfer.hint: “{{label}}” is an internal movement: the money left this account for another one. Point to the operation that received it — both will count as a single movement rather than as spending.
transfer.empty: No operation matches. The other account may be missing, or its statement not imported yet.

install.title: Install the app
install.iosInstructions: Tap Share, then “Add to Home Screen”.

recurring.title: Recurring expenses
recurring.description: Subscriptions, insurance, bills — anticipate what falls due and confirm each in one click.
recurring.emptyDescription: Add a subscription or bill to anticipate your cash flow.

confirm.title: Confirm this expense
confirm.hint: Records the expense in your journal and moves the schedule to the next occurrence. Adjust the amount if the bill changed.

report.title: Monthly report
report.description: A written recap of last month’s spending, budget by budget.
report.emptyDescription: Your first monthly report will appear once a month has closed with expenses.

access.hint: Written recap of last month’s spending.

compliance.cleanHint: Every operation is accounted for or arbitrated. Nothing left hanging.
compliance.openHint: Each one is either resolved, or arbitrated with a motive.
compliance.blockedBy: This check only covers accounts whose “{{prerequisite}}” prerequisite is cleared.
compliance.revoked: Arbitration revoked — the discrepancy is back.
compliance.waiveHelp: An arbitration erases nothing: it records why this discrepancy is acceptable. It stays visible and revocable.
compliance.reasonPlaceholder: E.g. bank fees, belongs to no budget
compliance.noDetectorsHint: Declare an account so the control has something to verify.

transaction_unallocated.title: Unaccounted outflows
transaction_unallocated.hint: Money left without anyone saying what for.
transaction_unallocated.resolution: Sort these from the “To sort” tab, or arbitrate them with a motive.

transaction_partially_allocated.title: Partly accounted outflows
transaction_partially_allocated.hint: Part of the amount is attached to nothing.
transaction_partially_allocated.resolution: Complete the split, or arbitrate the remainder.

expense_unreconciled.title: Unreconciled expenses
expense_unreconciled.hint: Typed into the app, never confirmed by a statement.
expense_unreconciled.resolution: Attach them to the matching bank line, or arbitrate them (paid by someone else, for instance).

account_chain_broken.title: Broken balance chain
account_chain_broken.hint: The statement balances do not chain: operations are missing.
account_chain_broken.resolution: Import the missing statement. Until then the balance stays flagged as unreliable.

account_cash_negative.title: Cash account in the red
account_cash_negative.hint: Physically impossible: a withdrawal was never declared.
account_cash_negative.resolution: Declare the withdrawal that feeds this account, from the bank journal (“Feed cash” on the withdrawal line).

expense_without_budget.title: Expenses outside any budget
expense_without_budget.resolution: Assign a budget, or arbitrate if it is deliberate.

inflow_unclassified.title: Unclassified receipts
inflow_unclassified.hint: Wage, refund or internal transfer? The three do not mean the same thing.
inflow_unclassified.resolution: Classify the receipt from the bank journal, or arbitrate if it has no bearing.

internal_without_counterpart.title: Internal movements with no counterpart
internal_without_counterpart.hint: The money left the tracked world and nothing accounts for it.
internal_without_counterpart.resolution: Create the counterpart (“Feed cash”), or clear the “internal” flag if it was not one.

recurring_overdue.title: Recurrences past due
recurring_overdue.hint: The treasury projection and the “committed” figure lie until the due date advances.
recurring_overdue.resolution: Confirm the occurrence, let the next statement do it, or arbitrate if the debit stopped.

recurring_double_confirmed.title: Recurrences confirmed twice
recurring_double_confirmed.hint: The same bill counted twice on the same day.
recurring_double_confirmed.resolution: Delete the duplicate occurrence from the Expenses tab.

statement_period_gap.title: Uncovered periods
statement_period_gap.hint: A month no statement ever covered — invisible to the balance chain check.
statement_period_gap.resolution: Import the missing statement, or arbitrate if there was no operation.

import_skipped_lines.title: Skipped lines to verify
import_skipped_lines.hint: The file had neither reference nor balance: dedup cannot be certain.
import_skipped_lines.resolution: Check the skipped lines really were duplicates, then arbitrate.

account_without_window.title: Account outside the control's reach
account_without_window.hint: No conformity window: either the opening balance is missing, or its date is later than your statements.
account_without_window.resolution: Set the opening balance date to the beginning of the period you imported — not to today. The amount should be the balance at that date: if it is approximate, only the displayed balance suffers, sorting your operations still works. Until the date is fixed, no other check covers this account.

account_anchor_stale.title: Attested balance no longer adds up
account_anchor_stale.hint: The opening balance was reconstructed from a balance you read. The arithmetic no longer closes.
account_anchor_stale.resolution: Operations have changed since. Import the missing statement, or read your balance again and rebuild it: while the gap stands, every balance on this account is off by the same amount.

refund_without_budget.title: Refunds crediting no envelope
refund_without_budget.hint: This money came back, but no budget takes it: the month's counter stays inflated by that much.
refund_without_budget.resolution: Pick the budget credited back from the bank journal, or arbitrate if this refund concerns no envelope.

refund_partially_allocated.title: Partially credited refunds
refund_partially_allocated.hint: Part of what came back credits no envelope: those budgets' counters stay inflated by that much.
refund_partially_allocated.resolution: Complete the split from the queue, or arbitrate if the remainder concerns no envelope.

cash_mirror_partial.title: Withdrawals only partly poured into cash
cash_mirror_partial.hint: Part of the withdrawal is neither a spend nor declared cash: that money belongs nowhere.
cash_mirror_partial.resolution: Correct the share that entered the cash pot, or arbitrate if the rest went elsewhere (own pocket, another household).

compliance.blockedHint: A prerequisite stops the checks from covering your accounts. Fix it and everything becomes measurable.

window.noDate: No opening balance date is set.
window.afterData: Your opening balance date is {{openingDate}}, but your oldest operation is {{earliestLine}}: the checking period is empty.

compliance.cashMissing: {{outflow}} withdrawn, {{mirrored}} poured into cash — {{missing}} belongs nowhere.

pending.allDoneHint: Every operation is accounted for or arbitrated.
pending.nothingLeftHint: Postponed operations will be back on your next visit.
pending.blockedHint: A prerequisite blocks the control: {{prerequisite}}. Your operations exist, but no rule can cover them yet.

expense.noBudget: No envelope — this expense counts in no category.
expense.notReconciled: No statement line justifies this expense yet.
expense.deleteConfirm: Delete this expense? It will disappear from the journal and from budget totals.
expense.deleteSplitConfirm: Delete this expense? The bank transaction is untouched: its amount goes back to the queue.

new.title: Record an expense
new.label: Label
new.pendingHint: No account line is created: the expense will be matched when you import the next statement.

refundExpense.title: This expense was refunded
refundExpense.description: Credits the {{budget}} envelope back. The expense itself stays unchanged.
refundExpense.amountHint: What goes back into {{budget}}. Leave the full amount for a cancelled order, lower it for a partial refund.
refundExpense.none: No incoming line can carry this refund yet. Import the statement, or classify the receipt as a refund first.

recap.title: Recap
recap.description: Your household's month, told in a few cards.
recap.emptyDescription: Your first recap will arrive on the 5th working day of the month, once a month has closed.

story.unavailable: Nothing to tell for this month
story.unavailableDescription: This month has too little recorded to make a recap.

delivery.title: The appointment
delivery.linkFirst: Link your Telegram account to get the recap.
delivery.enable: Tell me when a recap is ready
delivery.hint: Sent on the 5th working day of the month, on the month that just closed — the first days give you time to record everything. Off by default: if you also get the monthly budget report, you would receive two messages that morning.

chapters.title: Chapters
chapters.description: Turn off what you would rather not be told. Muting a chapter never erases it — turn it back on and past months read in full again.

suppliers.willBeAdded: New supplier — it will be added

capabilities.title: What this instance can do
capabilities.description: The capabilities this server has, based on the keys it was given.

assistant.name: Assistant
assistant.unavailable: The assistant is not configured on this instance.
assistant.without: Without a provider key the assistant cannot answer. Everything else in Maisonnée works, including keyword search.
assistant.enabled: The assistant answers questions about your household.

semantic_search.name: Semantic search
semantic_search.unavailable: Semantic search is not configured on this instance.
semantic_search.without: Keyword search still answers; only the results found by meaning are missing.
semantic_search.enabled: Search also finds things by meaning, not just exact words.

recap_ai.name: Recap wording
recap_ai.unavailable: Recap rewriting is not configured on this instance.
recap_ai.without: The monthly recap is still produced, with its built-in wording.
recap_ai.enabled: The monthly recap captions are rewritten in everyday language.

email.name: Outgoing email
email.unavailable: No mail server is configured on this instance.
email.without: Emails are written to the server log. You can still add members: the invitation link is copied by hand.

push.name: Push notifications
push.unavailable: Push notifications are not configured on this instance.
push.without: Notifications stay inside the app; nothing reaches a phone while it is closed.

telegram.name: Telegram
telegram.unavailable: The Telegram channel is not configured on this instance.
telegram.without: The Telegram channel is off. Notifications stay inside the app.
telegram.enabled: Your household can talk to the assistant from Telegram.

hunt_riddles.name: Hunt riddles
hunt_riddles.unavailable: Riddle writing is not configured on this instance.
hunt_riddles.without: Treasure hunts work exactly the same — you write the riddles yourself.
hunt_riddles.enabled: The assistant can propose a riddle for each room of a hunt.

project_assistant.name: Guided project creation
project_assistant.unavailable: Guided project creation is not configured on this instance.
project_assistant.without: Projects are still created with the form, exactly as before — nothing is missing.
project_assistant.enabled: The assistant asks a few questions, then proposes the project with its tasks and notes.

orchard.title: Orchard

empty.title: No subject in the orchard yet
empty.description: Add your trees, bushes and vines to track their care and their harvests.
empty.noZone: Create an outdoor zone first: every orchard subject belongs to a place.

fields.name: Name
fields.plantedOnHint: Leave empty if you do not know it.
fields.title: Title

errors.zoneRequired: Pick a zone: a subject with no place is a subject nobody finds again.
errors.floweringIncomplete: Set both the start and the end of flowering, or neither.

series.title: Harvests by season
series.singleSeason: One season is not a comparison yet — fruit trees alternate.

orchard.floweringPrompt: The flowering window is not set: without it, no frost alert can target this subject.

care.missedHint: Window closed — pick it up next season.
care.windowHint: A window may cross New Year — « November → March » is the normal shape in an orchard.

games.title: Treasure hunt
games.emptyDescription: Pick a few rooms, write a riddle for each, hide something at the end — and hand over the phone.
games.composerHint: The order of the steps is the order of the game. Each riddle should point at the room that comes next.
games.riddlePlaceholder: I am where the water sings in the morning…
games.treasurePlaceholder: The cake is in the switched-off oven
games.noActiveDescription: Start one from the hunt list, then hand the phone to the players.
games.noRiddle: No riddle for this step — head to the next room.
games.scanHint: Scan the QR label in the room with your camera

scan.advanced: Found! Here comes the next riddle.
scan.finished: That was the last one — the treasure is yours!
scan.wrong_zone: Not here. Read the riddle again.

riddles.hint: The assistant writes one riddle per room. You can edit every one of them before saving.
riddles.needRooms: Pick the rooms first — the riddles are written from them.
riddles.done: Riddles suggested — read them over and adjust.
riddles.failed: The riddles could not be written. Try again, or write them yourself.

games.replayed: Hunt ready to play again, in a new order
